maya: Quick heads-up — ran an nsys trace against the 3.2.0 rollout because we saw a perf regression tied to KV prefetch. Theres an extra kernel-switch right after prefetch that correlates with the delta. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 (canary run). Thoughts on where to put NVTX spans to debug without blowing up trace size?

trace-bot: trace uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/trace/2065432100/nsys_run.nsight 

arnold: can you paste the exact nsys command you used and a tiny timeline snippet?

maya: sure — command:```nsys profile -o run.nsight --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=cpu ./run_inference.sh --model=redwood-v2 --batch=8```
mini timeline from the perfetto flame (per-request):`kv_prefetch (1.4ms) -> kernelA (0.5ms) -> kernel_select (0.2ms) -> kernelB (2.1ms) -> kernelC (3.9ms)`
The surprising bit is the extra `kernel_select` that only shows up on ~10% of requests and aligns with the regression.

dena: NVTX name hygiene is important. Propose stable, parseable names like: `rt:req=<rid>:kv:prefetch` and `rt:req=<rid>:kernel:<short-name>`. Keep rid to a short hex (8 chars) to avoid bloating strings. Also prefer separators that are easy to split (`:` and `|`).

julian: +1 on stable names. downside: full per-request spans explode trace size. We should sample. Options: 1) enable full per-request NVTX for canary hosts only, 2) sample 1/1000 requests in prod, or 3) enable when request latency > 50ms. For this bug we can flip canary to full.

maya: Agreed. For debugging window, enable per-request spans on canary, and in prod use sampling/threshold. Also note: many perf tools have NVTX string length limits — keep under 64 chars or they'll get truncated and groups become unusable.

arnold: Also add KV hit/miss annotation. Example: `nvtxRangePushA("rt:req=%s:kv:prefetch|hit", rid)` vs `...|miss`. That lets perf queries filter by hit/miss easily.

dena: sample RAII macro I want to land (pseudocode):
```c
char _nvtx_tag[64];
snprintf(_nvtx_tag, sizeof(_nvtx_tag), "rt:req=%s:kv:prefetch|%s", rid, hit ? "hit" : "miss");
nvtxRangePushA(_nvtx_tag);
// ...
nvtxRangePop();
```
Key rules: always push/pop on same thread, guard the snprintf to avoid overflow, and provide a no-op build flag for high-volume paths.

julian: we should also consider coarse-grained "switch" markers: only emit a tiny NVTX range when we see a kernel-selection event (i.e., kernel-switch) rather than wrapping every kernel. That keeps trace density down but marks the interesting moments.

maya: thats smart — emit `rt:req=%s:kernel_switch` at the selection boundary, and only expand to full per-kernel spans on sampled requests.

arnold: quick checklist so we have owners:
1) implement RVNVTX wrapper + RAII helper (ensures <64 char and safe snprintf) — maya will open PR.
2) add `kv:hit|miss` tags to prefetch path — julian owns.
3) add kernel_switch marker and sampling knob (1/1000 default) — dena owns.
4) run full nsys+perfetto on canary and compare flame diffs — maya will run tomorrow.

maya: I'll open PR today with the wrapper and default naming. Will include a unit that asserts nvtx string length < 64 and a small integration on canary. Target: PR today, perf run tomorrow morning.

trace-bot: deploy-bot: canary perf-2 updated, traces scheduled for 2065432300 window.
